claims.text: Spain imposed border controls on all air and sea travel from Italy for one month starting at midnight (22:00 GMT).
Italy previously introduced border restrictions after approximately 78,000 migrants entered the Spanish exclave of Ceuta from Morocco.
The Italian government stated its border controls would remain in place until at least August 15.
Spain's Supreme Court ruled that migrants stopped at sea while attempting to reach Ceuta or Melilla cannot be summarily returned to Morocco.
Nearly 1,400 minors remain in Ceuta following the migrant influx from Morocco.
Spanish Foreign Minister José Manuel Albares described Italy's border checks as a torpedo fired at the hull of European unity.
Official Spanish figures indicate that 70,000 of the 72,000 people who entered Ceuta have returned to Morocco.
The Moroccan Association for Human Rights and European Coordination for Human Rights in Morocco reported at least 141 deaths linked to the Ceuta crossings.
Morocco's interior ministry stated that 11 people died on its side of the border, all but one from drowning.
On June 16, an international law enforcement operation dismantled a Western Mediterranean smuggling network, resulting in 78 arrests.
The dismantled smuggling network generated over 24 million euros ($27 million) in profits while bringing more than 2,000 people into Spain.
A 14-year-old student fatally shot his grandparents at home and opened fire at Debsirin Nonthaburi School before taking his own life.
The shooter fired at least 26 bullets using a gun belonging to his grandfather and was found with 34 additional rounds of ammunition.
The Small Arms Survey estimated in 2017 that Thailand had 10.3 million civilian-owned firearms, representing about 15 guns per 100 residents.
The 14-year-old gunman shot his 73-year-old grandfather and 74-year-old grandmother at their flat around 05:00 local time.
Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul announced plans to introduce legislation allowing only on-duty government officials to carry firearms in public.
Thai media reported that a student died from injuries following the shooting, raising the death toll to eight including the gunman.
The Thai health department reported that nine wounded victims were in critical condition following the school attack.
A 2022 attack by a former policeman in northeastern Thailand killed 37 people, including 22 children.
Five school staff members, including teachers and administrators, were killed at Debsirin Nonthaburi School around 10:00 a.m.
Debsirin Nonthaburi School ordered all classes suspended from August 10 to August 14 following the shooting.
Confirmed Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo reached 4,053 with 1,850 deaths reported since mid-May.
Ituri province accounts for 87 percent of the ongoing Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, while North Kivu accounts for 11 percent.
World Health Organization vaccine experts recommended a clinical trial of the Ervebo vaccine to evaluate potential protection against the Bundibugyo Ebola strain.
The vaccine alliance Gavi maintains a global stockpile of 500,000 Ervebo vaccine doses.
The Africa CDC and WHO plan to launch studies to check whether the Bundibugyo Ebola virus strain is mutating due to its rapid spread.
Health officials intercepted a riverboat in Maluku to screen over 300 passengers following the death of a passenger exhibiting Ebola-like symptoms.
Democratic Republic of the Congo health data recorded 3,973 Ebola cases and 1,801 deaths as of August 4.
More than two-thirds of Ebola deaths in the Democratic Republic of the Congo are occurring in local communities rather than treatment centres.
The Africa CDC announced plans to deploy health workers door-to-door for active case searching in affected areas.
UNICEF reported that first-dose measles vaccinations among children in Mongbwalu dropped by 69 percent amid the Ebola outbreak.
Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, and Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement in Mecca.
The Mecca Joint Defence Agreement provides that an armed attack against any one of the three participating nations shall be regarded as an attack against them all.
Iranian parliament member Ebrahim Rezaei stated that a paper agreement with Turkey and Pakistan would not bring security to Saudi Arabia.
Yemen's Houthi rebels declared a maritime embargo against Saudi Arabia and targeted Saudi airports, oil facilities, and tankers in the Red Sea.
India announced that it is closely following the newly signed defence agreement between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkey.
An unidentified Turkish official stated that the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement is purely defensive in nature and not directed at any specific nation.
The India Meteorological Department issued a yellow alert for Delhi following widespread heavy rain across the city.
Authorities confirmed that schools in Delhi-NCR will remain open on August 8 despite heavy rainfall warnings.
Educational institutions in Ghaziabad, Meerut, and Baghpat were ordered closed until August 12 due to heavy movement of pilgrims during the Kanwar Yatra.
The India Meteorological Department issued a red alert for Delhi-NCR on August 7, forecasting moderate to heavy rain, thunderstorms, and lightning.
Rainwater flooded the subway near Badarpur Border Metro Station, severely restricting movement for commuters.
In the 24 hours up to 8:30 a.m. on August 7, Lodhi Road recorded 60.4 mm of rainfall, Safdarjung recorded 59.2 mm, and Ridge recorded 57 mm.
Delhi recorded 127 mm of rainfall during the first seven days of August, marking its wettest first week of August in 13 years.
Sector 17 in Faridabad recorded 119.4 mm of rainfall between midnight and 5:00 p.m. on August 7.
Rainwater entered the grounds of Safdarjung Hospital, causing movement difficulties for patients and attendants.
